recommendations.rationale: Separating residual tip motion from slow position settling needs a bounded projected-state probe at a saved state whose effective horizon matches an authorized horizon; this phase excludes numerical work, so defer until such a saved state is in scope.

No control-parameter change is supported by this evidence: raw weight magnitudes (e.g., tip_speed_scale_m_s = 0.02, terminal_tip_speed_weight = 0, holding_tip_speed_weight = 0) do not establish cost-term importance without contribution/scaling data, and no optimizer iteration traces are retained.

Treat the long synchronous solve times (mean_update_s 17.08 s vs a 0.01 s control period; 35/35 deadline misses) as a separate compute-efficiency question, since scheduling metadata states these misses do not inject physical simulated delay and cannot by themselves explain the settling shortfall.

Attribution of the User_Requested_Stop early terminations would need optimizer iteration traces and complete warm plans, which are not retained (control_snapshots.json absent); defer a request for that evidence to a scope that provides it.

attribution.reason: At the final sample the tip position error (0.00764 m) is within the 0.01 m reach/settling position limit while the tip speed (0.635 m/s) is about 30x the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit, and every displayed final-window speed (0.635-1.58 m/s) exceeds that limit. The observed shortfall therefore includes non-decayed tip motion, not position error alone.

The 0.05 s settling window spans t = 0.30-0.35 s, where tip position error starts at 0.058 m, above the 0.01 m limit, and only reaches 0.00764 m at the last sample, so position was out of tolerance for part of the required window. Position and speed shortfalls are co-present in the retained window; retained evidence does not rank them.

Scheduling metadata for this run states that synchronous controller calls complete before fixed-count backend steps and that wall deadline misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time. The 35/35 deadline misses and 17.08 s mean update are therefore compute-time observations, not a simulated-time delay of the tip.

34 of 35 updates stopped with User_Requested_Stop and 1 with Solve_Succeeded, but no optimizer iteration traces or full warm plans are retained, so early termination or cost-weight imbalance cannot be confirmed or excluded. Raw weight magnitudes alone do not establish cost-term importance.

Per-update GVS projection residuals and one-step projected-versus-backend comparisons are retained, but a bounded projected-model probe cannot explain an entire settling failure and cannot separate objective weighting, seed selection, horizon, and backend-model effects; retained evidence cannot confirm this as the settling cause.

facts.statement: Sampled final-window settling did not pass (sampled_settling_passed = false) against the configured criteria position_limit_m = 0.01 m, speed_limit_m_s = 0.02 m/s, window_s = 0.05 s.
Terminal tip position error 0.007642608585867386 m is below the reach tolerance 0.01 m, but terminal tip speed 0.6351726092425104 m/s is far above the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit.

In the displayed final window (t = 0.30 to 0.35 s) the maximum tip position error was 0.05813810428573256 m and the maximum tip speed 1.5810152739742807 m/s, both above the settling limits; the position error fell monotonically (0.0581, 0.0478, 0.0341, 0.0191, 0.0101, 0.00764 m) while the reconstructed tip speed stayed far above 0.02 m/s (0.862, 1.329, 1.477, 1.581, 0.776, 0.635 m/s).

All 35 updates were recorded as deadline misses against the 0.01 s control period (mean_update_s = 17.075238151415917 s), and optimizer status was User_Requested_Stop for 34 updates and Solve_Succeeded for 1.

limitations: Single execution with single-model comparisons; no closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal-attribution capability, so no dominant cause is established.
